scenario: AITA for leaving to see my GF when my sister told me not to when she was "in charge"? | My mom is gone for a class thing in another state, and my dad is on a business trip so its just me, my sister and my brother all alone in the house. My sister is 18, I am 17 and my brother is 12, I don't know why but my parents still felt the need to leave my sister "in charge" while they were both gone. My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. On Sunday I was gonna go out with my GF for dinner, and my sister stopped me saying that I can't leave. When asked its cause "she said so", I laughed at that and I thought she was joking but she just kept looking and I knew it was a joke. I told her she can boss (little brother's name) around but she can't boss me, and I went out with my GF. I guess my younger brother heard all the commotion and called mom saying we were "fighting" and when I came home and my mom called me she said that I'm grounded and have to dow what my sister says cause she's "in charge". I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My parents left for a class thing and a business trip, respectively, leaving me, my 18-year-old sister, and my 12-year-old brother at home. My sister was put in charge, which I guess is normal when parents are away. But apparently, she's been taking that responsibility a bit too seriously. She can make my little brother obey her, but she has a harder time with me. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave, and when I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." I laughed, thinking she was joking, but she wasn't. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had called our mom and said we were fighting. My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do what my sister says because she's "in charge." I protested, but my mom wasn't having it. I ended up dropping it because I didn't want to argue further. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by leaving despite my sister's objections. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. She's technically older, but only by a year. My parents left her in charge, which gives her some authority. However, she's been taking that role too seriously, especially with me. I went out with my girlfriend, which is something I wanted to do. My sister told me I couldn't, but I didn't take her seriously at first. When I realized she was serious, I stood my ground and left anyway. The conflict arose because my sister tried to exert her authority over me, and I refused to comply. My little brother saw this as a fight and told our mom, leading to me being grounded. I need to think about whether I should have respected my sister's authority in this situation. On one hand, she was put in charge by our parents, and they expect us to follow her instructions. On the other hand, she's only a year older than me, and I might feel that her authority isn't legitimate, especially if she's been abusing it. I also need to consider the consequences of my actions. By going out despite her objections, I caused a fight, which led to me being grounded. My little brother was involved, which added to the conflict. I wonder if there was a better way to handle this situation. Maybe I could have talked to my sister about her authority and why she was making that decision. Or perhaps I could have found a compromise, like going out but coming back earlier or something like that. Another thing to consider is the role of our parents. They left my sister in charge, but they also grounded me for not obeying her. Does that mean they support her authority, or do they think I should have more freedom? I also need to think about the bigger picture. Am I setting a precedent by not following my sister's instructions? If I keep doing that, will it cause more conflicts in the future? Or is this a one-time thing that I can learn from? In the end, I need to decide whether I was in the right or not. Did I act appropriately by asserting my independence, or should I have respected my sister's authority more? I think it's important to balance respect for authority with personal judgment. While my sister was in charge, I also have the right to make decisions about my own life, especially when it comes to spending time with my girlfriend. However, I should have communicated better with my sister and perhaps found a way to resolve the conflict without causing a fight. Overall, I might have been a bit too quick to dismiss my sister's authority, but I also feel that she was overstepping her bounds by trying to control me. It's a tricky situation, and I can see both sides of the argument.
